claims.statement: Normal monsoon predicted for current year; first quarter FY25 may be impacted by general elections
Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY25
Tissue culture revenue target of INR325 crores for FY25
Food business targeting double-digit growth, internal target closer to 15% for FY25
Retail business growth target north of 20% for FY25
Food business order book of INR335 crores at India level and INR1,000 crores at global consolidated level
Non-food order book of INR900 crores at consolidated level, including institutional contractor business and remaining government projects
Tissue culture business EBITDA margin over 30%
Management expects demand revival and pent-up demand in H2FY25 on back of good monsoon and government budget announcements
Management maintains FY25 revenue guidance of INR7,000 crores despite weak Q1
Margins expected to improve structurally over 2 years as government project revenue declines and retail mix increases
India order book INR1,000 crores; consolidated INR1,800 crores (INR1,000 crores Food, INR800 crores Hi-Tech and Plastics)
Global capex INR45 crores in Q1 FY25 vs depreciation INR60 crores; in line with usual trend
Utilization: Pipe 55-60% (75% in season), Drip/Sprinkler ~45% (55-60% in season)
Management to provide firmer FY25 guidance and FY26 outlook in October after Q2 results
Expect demand boost in H2FY25 from increased sowing areas and well spread monsoon
Focus on deleveraging and optimizing cash flow, anticipate revival in MIS, Pipes, Tissue Culture segments
Management expects at least 7-8% YoY revenue growth for FY25 vs original 10-12% target; aims to meet original EBITDA guidance despite revenue shortfall
Full-year export target is to cross INR500 crores with 28-30% growth; medium-term goal to double exports to INR1,000 crores in 3-4 years
Tissue culture EBITDA margin ~30%, expected to maintain for next 2-3 years as price hikes offset input cost inflation; drip irrigation 15-16% targeting 18%; piping 12-13%
JJM contract orders and new solar water pump orders to flow in H2 FY25, helping recover H1 revenue deficit
H1 maintenance capex ~INR94 crores, similar to last year; full-year maintenance plus small growth capex expected slightly better than last year
Tissue culture capacity from FY23 INR50 cr investment still has headroom beyond 20% output increase; food processing has sufficient capacity for 3-year growth without major new capex
Company expects strong performance in next few quarters in piping, solar systems and international sales
Company anticipates recovery in consumption and increased government capex
Expects Q4 FY25 to have significant positive growth vs last year; FY25 full-year revenue at par with FY24; FY26 bullish with high-teens sustainable revenue growth target
Expects revenue growth in high teens for FY26; EBITDA likely to grow ~20% if revenue grows 17% due to operating leverage
Received solar water pump orders worth ~INR100 crores with 30-day payment terms for 90%; expects completion in next couple of months
Completed 2.5m diameter pipe supply for desalination project; 14-16 similar projects expected in next 9-12 months
Q3 EBITDA higher than last year despite similar gross margin; saved discretionary SG&A costs; expects EBITDA margin improvement with high-teens revenue growth due to fixed cost absorption
Underutilized production capacities across businesses; no new borrowing planned for growth; expansion to be funded from internal accruals and receivable recovery
Focus on deleveraging, working capital efficiency and better cash flow
FY26 revenue growth target high teens (~18%+) with EBITDA growth 23-24% and debt reduction of at least INR400 cr
Minimum debt reduction target INR400 cr in FY26, could be INR400-500 cr
EPC project receivables INR750-800 cr; expect >50% collection in FY26, remainder in FY27
EPC receivables collection expected INR400-450 cr in FY26 from Karnataka, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh
Hi-tech EBITDA margin improved to 18.7% from 13.4% YoY in Q4 FY25; standalone Hi-tech EBITDA margin 15.6% vs 12.7%
Agro Processing margins to recover in FY26 with better mango/onion season and processing at reasonable price
No major capex needed for planned growth; only small product-line investments within depreciation
Adequate capacity for MIS and PVC growth; no significant capacity expansion required
Expect revival of demand for piping business in H2 FY26
Working capital cycle expected to optimise in coming quarters
Revenue growth guidance of north of 15% for FY26 maintained despite 5% growth in Q1
Target to double business in 3-4 years and 2.5-3x in 5 years at 15%+ CAGR
Piping segment to grow 15-17%, irrigation 12-14%, plastic sheet 8-10%, solar pumps substantial growth under KUSUM
Overall EBITDA target 13-15% for FY26, Hi-Tech 15-17%, Plastics 12-14%, Agro Processing 12-13%
Hi-Tech Agri EBITDA improved from 15.2% to 16.6% in Q1 FY26
Agro Processing EBITDA improved by 1.6% in Q1 FY26
Exports grew 40% from INR88 crores to INR130 crores in Q1 FY26
Solar pump sales crossed INR50 crores in Q1 FY26 vs less than INR2 crores same period last year
Government project receivables of INR500-700 crores expected to be recovered by mid-FY26
Total project receivables ~INR750 crores, INR350 crores expected before March 2026
Q1 FY26 capex INR44 crores vs depreciation INR68 crores; full year capex to remain in line with depreciation
Existing capacity sufficient for 2-3 years growth in pipe and drip without serious capex
Commercial production at new JFFFL bottling unit with leading beverage brand expected in Q3 FY26
Expect sustainable demand revival with higher consumption in H2 FY26 on account of GST 2.0 and good monsoon
FY26 revenue growth target above 15%
FY27 debt repayment of ~Rs. 200 crores due in September and major amount in March
Q2 EBITDA grew 43% vs 20% revenue growth; high-tech EBITDA margin ~19%, plastics double-digit, agro-processing improved to double-digit
Consolidated order book Rs. 1,900 crores; Rs. 1,500 crores to execute by March FY26, Rs. 400 crores by September FY27
Beverage bottling unit: first two lines by March FY26, adding Rs. 400-500 crores revenue at 65-75% utilization in full year; Phase II in H2 FY27
Tissue culture capacity to increase 50% over 3 years, nearly doubling size
Revenue contribution from JFFFL beverage bottling facility expected from Q4 FY26
Expect improved traction for piping business in Q4 FY26
Targets >15% revenue growth and >15% EBITDA growth for FY26; aims for 18-20% revenue and earnings growth in FY27
Plastic division Q3 EBITDA fell from Rs 42 cr to Rs 33 cr (margin 10.8% to 7.2%); half due to inventory loss, half due to lower volumes from extended rains
Government project receivables: expect Rs 125 cr net reduction in Q4, Rs 350-400 cr reduction in FY27
Tissue culture capacity doubling opportunity being evaluated
The India business is expected to leverage its established customer base and strategic collaborations to drive sustainable growth in the coming fiscal periods.
The Company's new venture in private label bottling of juice drinks and carbonated soft drinks offers substantial growth potential.
Strategic initiatives in new product development, private label partnerships, and geographic expansion are expected to further strengthen JFFFL's global footprint in the coming years.
Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account (Property, plant and equipments) and not provided for (net of advances) Rs 22.05 crore
Company expects improved policy continuity and revival of irrigation and infrastructure spending supporting stronger demand
Expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet with large debt repayment
Targets retail business growth above 15% in FY27
Plans to be PAT positive in FY27
Invested INR140 crores in beverage bottling lines in Dec-Mar quarters; discussing 3 more lines for FY27
Tomato processing plant with Japanese partner expected to start in January next tomato season
Two beverage lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4 FY26; 3 more lines planned for FY27
Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% in Q4 FY26 from 12.8% YoY; Hi-Tech margin 19.8% vs 17.5%
Hi-Tech EBITDA grew 22% YoY in Q4 FY26; full-year Hi-Tech EBITDA grew 26% on 20% revenue growth
Government project receivables reduced by INR80 crores in Jan-Mar and INR30 crores in April; expects substantial collection in FY27
Consolidated order book was ₹1,700 crore as of Q1 FY27 (Hi-Tech Agri ₹135 cr, Plastic ₹276 cr, Food/Agri ₹1,289 cr)
Company reiterates EBITDA margin guidance of around 14% standalone and 12.5% consolidated for FY27
Company expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27 and significantly stronger performance in second half
Management expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and aims to maintain margins at ~14% standalone and 12-13% consolidated

Project billing was ~Rs 24 cr in Q1; one large Pune water supply project has triple-digit billing remaining; other projects have ~Rs 40-50 cr left
Biochar plant recently started using agri waste (corn cob, cotton stalk, mango stones) to create soil conditioner and carbon credits; revenue impact from next fiscal
Company expects to recover EBITDA margin in the second half of the year
Expects H2 FY27 to be flattish year-on-year; positive growth possible if polymer prices ease by Dec-Mar
Targets 8-10% positive growth in piping for full FY27
Hi-Tech MI micro-irrigation margin at 18.8% in Q2 FY27; Plastics at ~9%, Food at ~12%
Medium-term target: Plastics segment margin towards 12%, Hi-Tech MI at 18-19%
Active government projects reduced to 7-8 from ~78; closed 15-20 projects in last 6 months
Expects project business to reach zero by end of FY28
Tomato JV: INR 30-40 crore in Q4 FY27 subject to asset acquisition closing by Dec
Beverage phase 2: ~INR 100 crore between March and June quarter
Biochar growth capex expected in FY28, not current fiscal
